newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-HOILES HOMERS TWICE AS ORIOLES END RANDY JOHNSON STREAK.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-HOILES HOMERS TWICE AS ORIOLES END RANDY JOHNSON STREAK.

text.p: Chris Hoiles hit two home runs and equalled a career high with six RBI as the Baltimore Orioles ended Randy Johnson's 16-game winning streak with a 13-3 romp over the Seattle Mariners on a rainy Thursday.

Johnson (4-1), who was trying to match the American League record of 17 straight wins held by Johnny Allen and Dave McNally, allowed five runs and six hits in six innings and lost for the first time since August 1, 1995.
He walked two and struck out 10, but did not return to the mound in the seventh following a 57-minute rain delay.
Johnson threw 120 pitches and fell to 3-6 lifetime against Baltimore. He did not speak to reporters after the game.
Hoiles was playing first base for the first time since June 8, 1991, filling in for Rafael Palmeiro.
"I was glad to contribute to the team," Hoiles said. "It was great to give Rafael the day off and win."
Mike Mussina (4-1) allowed a run and five hits in seven innings for his fourth straight win. He walked one and struck out eight in improving to 8-1 lifetime against the Mariners.

"I was more relaxed tonight," Mussina said. "Johnson was expected to win, everyone talked about this record. The rain always has an effect. Johnson didn't come back and pitch the same way he started."
"Mussina pitched a great game," Baltimore manager Davey Johnson said. "I was worried about the delay, but he came back and pitched outstanding."
"Mussina used all of his pitches well," said Seattle shortstop Alex Rodriguez. "He was painting the plate at times.

"It was a good ballgame through the fifth inning. Conditions out there were tough. Randy is a power pitcher. I don't want to make excuses for him, but it was tough going out there ... Weather was a factor for both teams."
Brady Anderson hit his third home run and scored twice for Baltimore, which has won eight of its last 10 games.
Russ Davis homered for Seattle.

In New York, Andy Pettitte bounced back from his first loss of the season to become the American League's second six-game winner and Bernie Williams had two hits and scored twice as the Yankees held on to beat the Texas Rangers 5-4.

Charlie Hayes had two hits including a solo homer in the bottom of the eighth as New York won its third straight and 14th of its last 19. The Yankees beat Texas at home for the 13th time in their last 15 meetings.

Pettitte (6-1), coming off Saturday's 2-1 loss at Kansas City, gave up three runs and seven hits in 7 1/3 innings with two walks and six strikeouts. Ex-Yankee Jimmy Key, now with Baltimore, is the American League's other six-game winner.
The Rangers, who lost their third straight, scored a run and loaded the bases in the ninth against closer Mariano Rivera, who struck out A.L. Most Valuable Player Juan Gonzalez to end the game.
In Cleveland, Juan Guzman allowed three hits over seven innings and Otis Nixon went 3-for-4 and scored twice as the Toronto Blue Jays held off the Indians 4-3.

Guzman (3-2) snapped a personal two-game losing streak. Paul Quantrill got the final two outs for his first major-league save since June 9, 1994 and his first in the American League since July 25, 1993, with the Red Sox.
Orlando Merced and Shawn Green each had two hits and drove in a run for the Blue Jays, who have won five of their last six.
In Boston, Paul Molitor's bloop single in the sixth capped a five-run rally as the Minnesota Twins held on for a 10-7 victory over the Red Sox.
Molitor and Brent Brede drove in three runs apiece for the Twins, who put the game out of reach with four runs in the eighth. Minnesota won for just the third time in its last 15 games.
Rudy Pemberton hit his first grand slam in the second inning and Tim Naehring added a three-run homer in the eighth to account for Boston's offence.
In Chicago, Norberto Martin homered and tied a career-high with four RBI and James Baldwin pitched five innings for his first win of the season as the White Sox defeated the Oakland Athletics 10-6.

Baldwin (1-4) allowed two unearned runs and two hits with two walks and six strikeouts. He didn't allow a hit until George Williams lined a ball off his right shoulder for an infield single with two out in the fifth. Baldwin finished the inning but suffered a contusion in his pitching shoulder and did not return for the sixth.
Mike Mohler (0-4) was tagged for eight runs and nine hits in 4 2/3 innings. He is winless in 18 career starts.
In Detroit, Tim Belcher and Hipolito Pichardo combined on a seven-hitter and Jay Bell homered to help the Kansas City Royals to a 4-0 victory over the Tigers.

Belcher (4-3) won his third straight start, allowing a season-low four hits over seven innings with four walks and five strikeouts. Pichardo allowed one hit over the final two innings, extending his streak of scoreless innings to 16.
